one_line_contribution: A measured upper bound on the query-agnostic memory-curation policy class -- LOO-best fixed configuration, a set-level outcome oracle prune, a GEPA static demonstration search, and a prompted sequential bank editor all land within a few points of volume-matched random selection, while a training-free query-conditional reranker at identical k clears them -- delivered together with the matched-volume random-removal control that the curation literature omits.
closest_prior_work: Two, and they threaten different halves. (1) arXiv:2603.02473 (retrieval-vs-utilization factorial) is the collider the proposal itself names, and it is correctly handled: it establishes the direction but never measures a ceiling, never replicates seeds, and never fixes injected volume, so the bound survives it. (2) The one the proposal underweights is classical query-conditional selection plus cross-encoder reranking: KATE (Liu et al. 2021) and Rubin et al. (2022) already establish that per-query demonstration retrieval beats a fixed demonstration set, and that a cross-encoder rerank of a bi-encoder top-k beats the bi-encoder ordering is a standard IR result. F6 is billed as the boldest claim in the paper, but as operationalized (C6 = cross-encoder rerank of top-12, inject top-4; C3 = delete 12 of 120 bank items, then bi-encoder top-4) it is a restatement of that IR result rather than a policy-class discovery. The proposal argues the novelty is the magnitude and the oracle-vs-untrained asymmetry; that argument only works if the two arms are matched on retrieval mechanism, and they are not.
strongest_objection: The Phase-1 centerpiece does not instantiate the policy class the title claims to bound, and the flaw pre-determines both poles of the result. All 8 configurations are rank patterns of size 4 over the BGE retriever's per-query top-12, so every so-called query-agnostic arm has already been conditioned on the query by the retriever before P1 chooses anything; P1 only picks which slice of an already-topically-relevant candidate list to inject. F1 (P1 - P0 <= 2) is therefore close to guaranteed by construction -- eight 4-subsets drawn from the same 12 retrieved items should differ little -- and confirming it says nothing about whether a policy that fixes bank contents before the query, which is exactly what A-MAC, SAGE, and Memory-R1 do, is bounded. The +-2.5 point CI is advertised as making the null informative, but precision on a quantity that is small by design is not evidence for the thesis. Symmetrically, F6's positive pole is confounded: C6 and C3 differ in retrieval mechanism (cross-encoder vs bi-encoder), not only in conditionality, and C3 is further crippled because deleting 12 of 120 items leaves the injected top-4 unchanged for roughly two-thirds of queries, mechanically compressing C1/C2/C3/C9/C10 differences toward the +-3 band that F5 predicts. Both the headline null and the headline positive are thus produced by design choices orthogonal to the claim about decide-before-query policies. A reviewer would write: the paper measures the flatness of the retriever's own top-12 and the well-known benefit of reranking, then reports it as a ceiling on write-time curation.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Add a genuinely query-agnostic arm to Phase 1: a fixed 4-item package injected for every instance, LOO-best over a pool of item sets with no retriever in the loop. That is the object the write-time literature actually ships, and only its ceiling can be reported as the ceiling on query-agnostic curation; the current rank-pattern P1 should be relabelled as a retrieval-slice ablation. (2) De-confound F6 with a 2x2: bi-encoder vs cross-encoder read-time selection crossed with full bank vs C3-pruned bank. If cross-encoder-on-pruned-bank equals cross-encoder-on-full-bank, that is the clean statement the paper wants; C6 vs C3 as written is not. (3) Sweep prune depth (12 / 36 / 60 / 90 of 120) and report, per Phase-3 condition, the fraction of the 600 instances whose injected top-4 actually changed. Without that number the +-3 nulls in F5 are uninterpretable, because a null under a 10% perturbation is not a null about curation. (4) Replace R2's pooled seed-noise 95th percentile with a per-instance within-instance configuration-label permutation null; seed variance is strongly instance-dependent (boundary instances flip regardless of configuration), so a global threshold will inflate the config-sensitivity fraction and pre-confirm F4. Note also that F4's interaction term is computed as a difference of variance estimates and is a residual bucket, so interaction >= 3x main effect is close to tautological once the main effect is small by design. (5) Raise the GEPA budget or drop the F7 wording: concluding from a 1,200-episode reflective search that the ceiling is a property of the class rather than the search budget invites the obvious rebuttal that the search was underpowered, and the proposal itself names C4 as the most dangerous refuting baseline.
missing_baseline: A no-memory (k=0) arm in Phase 3. It exists only as a 200-instance Phase-1 reference, yet the track's own prior result is that injecting a retrieved bank fixed zero items and broke six to seven; if C0 through C10 all sit at or below no-memory on the 600 held-out instances, every headline comparison in Phase 3 is a contest among conditions that are jointly worse than doing nothing, and the plan as written cannot detect that. Also omitted: a curation-depth sweep (everything is tested at 12 of 120 removed), a fixed-item static package in Phase 1 as described above, and a cross-encoder-reranked variant of each static condition to separate reranking from pruning in F6.
preprint_collision: Unusually strong in form and honest in substance -- it names arXiv:2603.02473 as a partial collision, concedes the directional novelty outright rather than arguing around it, states a decidable disagreement (C3 vs C2, P1 vs P0), and retracts a previously load-bearing citation it could not re-verify. I would credit that. But it has specific gaps that the proposal should not be allowed to treat as neutral. First, it never runs a search for the control it claims is universally absent: volume-matched or token-budget-matched deletion controls are most likely to already exist outside agent memory, in RAG context-compression, context-pruning, and lost-in-the-middle work, and the check queries only the memory-curation and read-time-memory neighbourhoods. The claim that no paper reports such a control is therefore under-searched in exactly the region where a collision would hurt most. Second, it reimplements A-MAC (arXiv:2603.04549) as C1 and calls it faithful while admitting it could only retrieve title and venue, not the abstract; a baseline whose method description was never read cannot carry a pre-registered fidelity check, and C1 vs C2 is one of the four conditions declared undroppable. Third, having already had to withdraw MEMAUDIT (arXiv:2605.02199) as unverifiable raises the prior that other IDs in the Related Work (2607.13591, 2606.24428, 2606.06240, 2608.02113) are cited from retrieval snippets rather than read, and the proposal does not say which of its citations it verified beyond metadata. Net: I can name no preprint that already measures this ceiling, so the bound's novelty stands; the direction's novelty is conceded and gone, and F6's novelty is threatened by the pre-2023 conditional-selection and reranking literature rather than by any 2026 preprint.
